newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOSTER'S RAISES STAKE IN INDIAN BREWERY.
newsitem.headline: FOSTER'S RAISES STAKE IN INDIAN BREWERY.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said on Thursday it had increased its interest in Aurangabad brewery, near the Indian city of Mumbai, to 74 percent from 51 percent after successfully lobbying the Indian government for approval.
India's Kothari Industrial Corp still retains a 24 percent stake and the remaining interest is held through an Indian nominee company, a Foster's spokeswoman said.

The construction of the A$18 million, 35 million litre a year brewery started earlier this year with the first stage of construction, bringing the brewery to an initial 10 million litre of capacity, seen completed by December.

"It is still early days for the Indian beer market, but all the signs are extremely promising. The market is certainly one in which good margins can be achieved on beer," Foster's chief executive, Ted Kunkel, said in a company newsletter.
Kunkel had previously said the group expected to make profits from the Indian venture within four years of the project's commencement date.
Fosters said Mumbai, with a population of 12.5 million, was one of the world's largest cities and was acknowledged as a thriving market for domestic and international consumer goods.

"Although beer consumption in India is only about a third of Australian consumption, a growing urban middle class is accounting for remarkable increases of more than 15 percent per annum," Foster's Asia chief operating officer Jim King said in the newsletter.

King said the state of Maharashtra in which Mumbai and Aurungabad are located, represents 23 percent of the total Indian beer market and has a greater number of relatively high income households than any other Indian state.
